turns.text: real quick big ask. tonight is my last 9pm overtime shift of the run. after that i wanna plan the week. i want to sleep a full night once its over, how do i schedule that without wrecking my body clock lol

Nice, that's a milestone. To shift your body clock back gradually, here's a simple plan:

- Monday: Finish your shift, then sleep a normal daytime block, but cap it at about 5-6 hours so you're tired by evening. Get outside in daylight after waking.
- Monday night: Go to bed around 10:30-11 p.m. Dim lights and put your phone away 30 minutes before.
- Tuesday onward: Aim for 7.5-8 hours at night, with a consistent wake time. Keep the same wake time even on weekends.

What time do your classes start and what are your work hours after this week? I can fit it to your actual schedule.
classes are afternoons mon wed thu 2-5:15. after tonight i think regular nights are back but not sure yet. just finished my 5 container chicken and rice prep btw so food is covered for the week

Nice, that's a solid base for the week. If you're back to regular nights you'll still need a plan, so here's one for now that works either way:

- Wake time: 8:30 a.m. for days with class, which leaves time to eat and get there for 2.
- Bedtime: 12:30 a.m. at the latest if you're on a day schedule; adjust if a night shift returns.
- Keep one "buffer" night this week with no early alarm.

If your shifts do come back, tell me the hours and I'll redo it.
ok. gym too. ive been down to 2 sessions a week during overtime. want to build back up to like 4 and get my strength back. whats the move, and what should i eat for it

Rebuilding methodically works best:

**Week 1:** Stay at 2 sessions but add a third lighter one late in the week. Use about 80-85% of your recent working weights to ease back in.
**Week 2:** Go to 3 full sessions.
**Week 3:** Add the 4th, e.g. an upper/lower split (Mon/Tue/Thu/Sat).

Track your top sets each session in a note so you can see progress and add 5 lb when all reps feel clean.

**Fuel:**
- Roughly 0.7-1 g protein per lb of bodyweight daily
- A carb-heavy meal 1-2 hours before lifting (rice, oats, banana)
- Protein within a couple of hours after
- Sleep matters as much as food for rebuilding, so your full nights help

Want me to put the protein targets into your meal prep, or just give you a short checklist?
short checklist pls. also add groceries for thanksgiving. im doing mac and cheese at my moms duplex

Short version:

**Weekly checklist**
- Chicken + rice prep: done ✅
- Add eggs, oats, bananas, Greek yogurt for breakfasts and pre-lift snacks
- Protein shake or milk post-workout
- Lift days: 4, track top sets
- Wake time fixed, 7.5-8 hrs sleep

**Thanksgiving mac and cheese (serves ~8-10):**
- 1 lb elbow macaroni
- 16 oz sharp cheddar (block, shred it yourself)
- 8 oz Colby Jack or Monterey Jack
- 4 cups whole milk
- 4 tbsp butter, 4 tbsp flour
- Smoked paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper
- Breadcrumbs or crushed crackers for topping

Check your mom's kitchen for a big baking dish and buy the cheese early in the week. Want it split into two shopping trips?
lol ok that helped. one trip midweek is fine. thanks
Sounds good. Midweek trip, one list. Enjoy the full night of sleep after tonight, you've earned it. Good luck with the last shift!
